target.title: fix(codex): use UTF-16-safe truncation for approval display paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The codex app-server approval and elicitation bridges truncate user-provided text (command previews, approval titles, display parameter values) using raw `String.prototype.slice`. When the truncation boundary falls between the high and low surrogate of a supplementary-plane character (emoji, CJK extension, etc.), the output contains a lone surrogate — corrupted UTF-16.

This is the same class of bug fixed in #99566 for `exec-approval-command-display.ts`. The shared `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` helpers (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`) already back off from split surrogate pairs at the boundary; they are used by 20+ other extensions but were not yet adopted in these three codex bridge files.

Relates to gap finding: `codex-utf16-safe-truncation` (`utf16-boundary`, evidence level A)
Location: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-bridge.ts:1498`

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace raw `String.prototype.slice` with `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` in all 6 call sites across 3 source files:

| File | Function | Cap | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `truncate()` | 48–180 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `previewSource()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `appendPreviewPart()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `elicitation-bridge.ts` | `sanitizeDisplayText()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `elicitation-bridge.ts` | `truncateDisplayText()` | 120 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |
| `plugin-approval-roundtrip.ts` | `truncateForGateway()` | 80, 256 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |

The SDK helpers are dependency-free, already exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, and already in use within the same extension (`node-cli-sessions.ts:698`). Cap sizes, truncation markers, and redaction order are unchanged.

## User Impact

Affects codex app-server users whose command previews or approval display text contain emoji or other astral-plane characters near the truncation boundary. Before this fix, a dangling high surrogate could appear in approval prompts; after, the emoji is dropped as a unit and the preceding character is preserved.

## Evidence

### 1. Transport-layer roundtrip proof — real terminal output captured via script(1)

Transport-layer test uses `CodexAppServerClient.fromTransportForTests` with a `PassThrough`-backed fake transport to exercise the **real JSON-RPC code path** that a spawned codex app-server process traverses. The client's `readline.createInterface` parses frames, `handleParsedMessage` → `handleServerRequest` dispatches, handlers run the full approval/elicitation bridge with emoji at truncation boundaries, and `writeMessage` routes results back.

**Real terminal capture** (`script -q -c "..." /tmp/proof-codex-transport-roundtrip.log`):

```
$ script -q -c "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-bridge.transport-roundtrip.test.ts \
  -- --reporter verbose 2>&1" /tmp/proof-codex-transport-roundtrip.log

======================================================================
Transport-layer roundtrip proof — Codex app-server approval & elicitation bridges
======================================================================

[transport] initialize handshake OK

[proof] command approval: 182 code units, emoji at 176-177
[proof] approval response: decision=accept
[proof] all approval event fields: clean UTF-16

[proof] elicitation param: 312 code units, emoji at 300-301
[proof] elicitation response: clean UTF-16

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Code paths exercised** (vs. handler-level tests which call `handleCodexAppServerApprovalRequest` directly):

- `handleLine` → `JSON.parse` frame parsing (real `readline` interface)
- `handleParsedMessage` → `handleServerRequest` dispatch
- `runServerRequestHandlers` → registered approval/elicitation handler
- Handler returns result → `writeMessage` → appears on transport stdin

This is the **exact same pipeline** that processes `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` and `mcpServer/elicitation/request` messages from a real codex app-server process. The fake transport's stdout/stdin simulate the child process streams; the client code under test is the real production client.

### 2. Handler-level unit tests — 115 passed

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-bridge.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/elicitation-bridge.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

Two new regression tests assert zero lone surrogates in both approval events and gateway request payloads after `handleCodexAppServerApprovalRequest` and `handleCodexAppServerElicitationRequest` process emoji-boundary inputs.

### 3. Full suite combined — 118 passed

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  118 passed (118)
```

### 4. Lint / format / review

- `oxlint` on all changed files — **clean**
- `oxfmt --check` — **clean**
- Autoreview: **no findings**

### 5. Codex environment

- `codex` v0.142.5 installed; `codex doctor` shows DeepSeek provider reachable at `http://127.0.0.1:4446/v1`
- Auth is present for the active provider
- This machine can run real codex agent turns — the transport-layer test proves the fix works through the same JSON-RPC dispatch path

### Summary

| Evidence Layer | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Transport roundtrip | Real client → JSON-RPC dispatch → handler → response | **3/3 passed** |
| Handler tests | Real entry points + full truncation pipeline | **115/115 passed** |
| Combined suite | All 3 test files | **118/118 passed** |
| oxlint | Changed files | **clean** |
| Autoreview | Full PR diff | **no findings** |

Behavior addressed: every truncation call site in approval-bridge.ts, elicitation-bridge.ts, and plugin-approval-roundtrip.ts.

Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/codex-utf16-safe-truncation`, commit `742aec8`, codex 0.142.5 installed and authenticated.

Observed result after fix: transport-layer roundtrip sends emoji-boundary JSON-RPC approval and elicitation requests through the real client dispatch → handler → truncation pipeline; responses and approval events contain zero lone surrogates.

What was not tested: real end-to-end codex agent run with an LLM that produces emoji in command output (requires a real codex agent session with a model that inserts emoji near truncation boundaries — this would only produce different coverage if the model-generated text happens to place an emoji at exactly the boundary positions already tested).
